keyframe_review.note: New keyframe -100 to 800: the page places the culture on 'the arid, southern coast of Peru' in 'the Rio Grande de Nazca drainage and the Ica Valley'; the infobox says today it lies in the Ica Department. No area is given.

ledger.note: c. 100 BCE: the Nazca culture begins on the south coast of Peru. Infobox 'Established: 100 BCE'; 'flourished from c. 100 BC to 800 AD' (Proto Nazca 100 BC-1 AD). Preceded by the Chavín and Paracas cultures.

region.text: the Ica Department: the Río Grande de Nazca drainage and the Ica valley

ledger.note: c. 800: the Nazca culture ends. Infobox 'Disestablished: 800 CE' while the text says 'by 750 AD the civilization had fallen completely'; Cahuachi's ceremonial use ended around 450-500 (Cahuachi page: severe drought, mudslides and earthquakes). Power shifted to the highlands with the Wari, dated about 650.

wars.name: Wari rise over the Nazca coast
wars.outcome: No fighting recorded: the page only says power 'shifted from the coast to the highlands with the Wari culture' (about 650); the Huari page calls Nasca 'under heavy Wari influence'.
wars.note: Listed so the reviewer sees it was considered.

sources.title: Nazca culture
sources.note: Dates 100 BCE-800 CE, Ica department, Rio Grande de Nazca drainage and Ica valley, chiefdoms, decline, succeeded by Wari c. 650.

sources.title: Cahuachi
sources.note: Ceremonial centre based c. 1-500 CE, abandoned around 450-500 (Orefici), not a capital.

notes: A culture: 'Early Nazca society was made up of local chiefdoms and regional centers of power' and Cahuachi was 'a non-urban ceremonial site', not a capital, so identity.capitals is empty. The page's end dates conflict (infobox 800, text 750); the Wari rise is dated about 650. Paracas (before 100 BCE) has no dossier. Cahuachi page: based about 1-500 CE, abandoned around 450-500. The Pisco valley is not named on the page.
